title: Find the aisle number
scenario: These aisle numbers are sorted smallest to biggest. Find where 30 sits — without scanning them one by one.

intro.job: These aisle numbers are sorted smallest to biggest. Find where 30 sits — without scanning them one by one.

idea.rule: Check the last aisle standing — the search runs while lo is still at or below hi, not just below.
idea.detail: Binary search keeps two fingers, lo and hi, around the part of the list that could still hold the target. Look at the middle: too small means the target is to the right (lo = mid + 1), too big means it's to the left (hi = mid - 1). Each look halves what's left. When lo and hi land on the same aisle, that aisle still needs checking — so the loop runs while lo <= hi.

watch.code:
nums, target = pair
lo = 0
hi = len(nums) - 1
found = -1
while lo <= hi:
    mid = (lo + hi) // 2
    if nums[mid] == target:
        found = mid
        break
    elif nums[mid] < target:
        lo = mid + 1
    else:
        hi = mid - 1
print(found)

model_restatement: Find the position of the target in the sorted list by halving, and print it — or -1 if it isn't there.

clarify.question: What if the target isn't on any aisle?
Can a number appear twice?
clarify.answer: No — every aisle number is different.

clarify.question: Can I just scan from the front?
clarify.answer: It would work — but the job is to halve, not scan.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Keep lo and hi around the search area. While lo is below hi, look at the middle and move lo or hi toward the target. Print where you found it, or -1.

why_line: After two looks, lo and hi both sit on aisle 5 — but 'while lo < hi' is already False, so aisle 5 (the 30) is never checked and found stays -1.

explain.rule: lo < hi stops the search when exactly ONE aisle is left — the very aisle that might hold the answer — so the last aisle standing never gets looked at.
explain.bridge: When lo and hi point at the same aisle, should the search stop or look?

fix.rule: while lo <= hi: keep looking while there's at least one aisle left, including the last one.

walk.gloss: Keep going while there's at least one aisle in range — even just one.
Too small — the target is to the right, so drop everything up to mid.
